def factor_overnight_gap_pressure_vol(df):
    """Overnight downside gap persistence amplified when gap occurs on elevated volume."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    prev_close = df_copy["close"].shift(1)
    overnight_log_ret = np.log(df_copy["open"] / prev_close.replace(0, np.nan))
    downside_gap = np.minimum(overnight_log_ret, 0.0)
    overnight_pressure = -downside_gap.rolling(20, min_periods=5).mean()
    _high_vol, _low_vol, vol_ratio = alpha_tools.classify_volume_regime(df_copy["volume"], window=20)
    volume_confirmation = np.clip(vol_ratio, 0.7, 1.3)
    fragility = overnight_pressure * volume_confirmation
    fragility.name = "factor_overnight_gap_pressure_vol"
    return fragility
description: Preserves the parent's core economic mechanism: persistent overnight downside gaps indicate idiosyncratic fragility after industry/size neutralization. This mutation replaces the close-location modifier with a volume-regime bounded attenuation. The active classify_volume_regime tool gives vol_ratio = volume / EMA(volume, 20); clipping vol_ratio to [0.7, 1.3] amplifies the raw overnight-gap pressure when gaps occur on elevated volume and dampens it on quiet volume. The modifier is continuous and bounded, so the returned signal remains cross-sectionally rankable. The target is to sharpen top-quantile crash fragility while retaining the parent's downside-gap persistence mechanism.
